This PR lands the adjudication mechanism on trusted main only. It does not itself adjudicate PR #1287's stale COMMENTED review (PRR_kwDOPyIw988AAAABLPwIjQ, 29 commits behind #1287's current head) — that is an explicitly separate, HOLD-gated follow-up per the originating directive (POST_ADJUDICATION_TO_PR1287=HOLD), not performed as part of this proof.

Running `pytest tests/pr_steward/ -q .` (trailing dot / broadened rootdir) pulls in unrelated duplicate-basename test trees and fails at collection; this is a pre-existing repo-wide pytest-invocation hazard unrelated to this change, surfaced during the independent audit. The correct scoped invocation is `pytest tests/pr_steward/ -q`.

The dedup key for conflicting receipts is the raw comment body string (exact bytes). A trusted approver's receipt that is edited after posting (same GitHub comment id, different body on refetch) is evaluated against whatever body the harvest captured at run time; this mechanism does not track edit history, consistent with the rest of the classifier's real-time-snapshot design.

AGY finding F-ADJ001-AGY-INFO-1: a trusted approver cannot use this mechanism to clear a COMMENTED review from an unknown/untrusted reviewer, because the unknown-author check runs before the receipt lookup is ever reached. Narrows the mechanism's documented scope; fail-closed, not a vulnerability. ACCEPTED_RISK, no code change made.

AGY finding F-ADJ001-AGY-INFO-2: a multi-line reason= value in a receipt is silently truncated to its first line by the per-line field regex; the receipt still clears the review correctly, only the recorded rationale text loses trailing context. ACCEPTED_RISK, no code change made.

findings.title: Conflict-detection dedup keyed on parsed fields + adjudicator, not raw bytes
findings.body: Found by the preceding Codex round-1 review, fixed in af145c4b1, independently re-verified fixed by this AGY run (invariant 5 in AUDITOR_REPORT.md: distinct_bodies set comprehension over raw comment bytes, classifier.py:1434-1441). Original _find_review_adjudication built its conflict-detection signature from (review_id, head_sha, disposition, reason, adjudicator), which let two receipts with different raw comment bytes but identical parsed fields wrongly dedupe as one (false clearance), and made two byte-identical receipts from two different trusted approvers wrongly conflict (false denial). Covered by test_byte_identical_body_from_two_different_trusted_authors_is_not_a_conflict and test_same_parsed_fields_but_different_raw_bytes_is_a_conflict, both spot-checked by this AGY run against the classifier logic by hand.

findings.title: Unknown-author precedence narrows the mechanism's usable scope
findings.body: A trusted approver cannot adjudicate a COMMENTED review from an unknown/untrusted reviewer, because _classify_reviews's _known_author check (classifier.py:552) assigns UNKNOWN_REVIEWER_NEEDS_CLASSIFICATION before the else branch that would consult a receipt (line 565) is ever reached. Narrower than the mechanism's stated scope, but fail-closed in the safe direction (no false clearance). No code change made.

findings.title: Multi-line reason= text silently truncated to its first line
findings.body: _parse_review_adjudication_receipt tokenizes via body.splitlines() and matches ^(review_id|head_sha|disposition|reason)=(.*)$ per line, so a multi-line reason keeps only its first line. The receipt still correctly clears the review; only the recorded rationale text loses trailing context. No false clearance or false denial. No code change made.
